item.title: Wearables for Biomechanics
item.description:
In the field of musculoskeletal (MSK) disease management, the role of biomechanics cannot be overstated. Biomechanics, the study of the mechanical forces and movements that occur within the human body, plays a pivotal role in understanding and improving the functioning of the musculoskeletal system. This is particularly crucial in the context of musculoskeletal diseases, such as knee osteoarthritis (KOA), which often require targeted approaches to restore mobility and enhance quality of life.

Our group recognize the significance of biomechanics in musculoskeletal disease management, specifically in the domain of KOA gait re-training. Gait re-training, a therapeutic intervention aimed at modifying abnormal walking patterns, has shown promising results in managing KOA. However, accurately assessing and quantifying biomechanical metrics during gait re-training has remained a challenge, hindering the optimization of treatment strategies.

To address this challenge, our interdisciplinary team is at the forefront of developing novel solutions that combine wearable sensing technologies with deep learning techniques. By integrating the power of wearable devices and advanced machine learning algorithms, we aim to enable precise and real-time estimation of biomechanics metrics for musculoskeletal disease management.

Our research methodology centers around leveraging deep learning-enhanced wearable sensing technologies to gain valuable insights into the biomechanics of individuals with musculoskeletal diseases, with a specific focus on KOA gait re-training. This approach offers several key advantages:

  1. We employ state-of-the-art wearable devices, such as inertial measurement units (IMUs) and smart textiles, to capture high-resolution data on joint angles, forces, and movement patterns. These non-invasive and unobtrusive sensors allow us to collect biomechanical data in real-world settings, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of gait dynamics.

  2. Through the application of state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms, we harness the computational power necessary to analyze complex biomechanical data. By training neural networks on large datasets, we can extract meaningful patterns and relationships, facilitating accurate estimation of key biomechanical metrics for disease management.

  3. With a strong connection with professional MSK disease clinicians and patients, we have the ability to identify real clinical demands and facilitate wearable sensing technology transfer from laboratory to clinics or home, trying to enable precise MSK disease management.

By combining cutting-edge wearable sensing technologies with deep learning techniques, our team strives to revolutionize the field of disease rehabilitation. Our ultimate goal is to improve the outcomes of musculoskeletal disease management, particularly in the context of KOA gait re-training, by providing clinicians and patients with accurate and actionable biomechanical insights.
